content:
I've been using Git for quite some time now to manage my projects and build up my portfolio. But to be honest, up until recently, I didn't really care about understanding the depths of it. Most of my tasks were just handled by copying and pasting whatever commands an LLM gave me. 

But I realized I can't stay complacent with that approach anymore, for a few big reasons:

1. **Mindless execution is risky.** Just running commands without actually knowing what they do is a recipe for disaster. Haha, I actually once executed a command that deleted core OS files on a Linux system and wiped out everything, just because I copy-pasted code an AI gave me. I mean, it's not the end of the world since Linux is open-source and you can just reinstall it for free, but the setback is the sheer amount of time it wastes.
2. **Real collaboration changes things.** I've worked on projects with friends before, but I never *really* understood true collaboration until I started working on an actual, large codebase. 
3. **It's an essential daily tool.** Git is incredibly popular and standard practice in almost every company. Learning the fundamentals isn't about flexing; it's purely about making my day-to-day tasks smoother.

With all that in mind, I tried diving into the learning material. I looked at a ton of different resources, but I ended up giving up on most of them because they just weren't engaging. They were dry, boring, and I kept losing interest midway through. 

Then, I stumbled across a post pointing me toward this resource: https://learngitbranching.js.org/

And honestly? Like, *really*... I am amazed. I managed to fly through it in just two days. My level of understanding of Git is definitely higher now, and it feels like a small yet super satisfactory achievement. I actually rushed right over here to write this post because of it! 

I'll leave you guys with the link to explore it yourself. If you end up liking the resource, send me a note on my socials! Hahaha, the more people get to use it, the better. 

See ya again soon...
